reason: Prepare the additional membrane needed for cell growth and division.
expectation: The phospholipids and proteins will form new membrane material, though I am unsure how it will be incorporated.

alternatives.reason: Copying DNA is also a goal, but I chose to prepare the membrane first.

effect: The membrane supply is packaged in vesicles routed through the ER and Golgi; it can now enlarge the cell.
reaction: The delivery route makes the membrane-building step clearer.
reason: Use the newly prepared vesicles to meet the cell-enlargement goal.
expectation: The vesicles will deliver membrane to the cell surface, allowing the cell to grow.

alternatives.reason: DNA copying is also necessary, but I want to finish the membrane route first.

effect: The cell has grown by adding membrane, but its nuclear DNA still needs copying.
reaction: The fusion inset clearly connects vesicle delivery to cell growth.
reason: Copy the nuclear DNA so the cell can eventually give each daughter a complete genome.
expectation: The nucleotides will be used to copy the cell's nuclear DNA.

alternatives.reason: The spindle is also needed, but copying DNA first follows the cell's current state.

effect: The grown cell now has copied nuclear DNA, and a spindle is needed to form two daughter nuclei.
reaction: The sister-chromatid inset makes the copied state visible.
reason: Build the spindle needed for the new goal; it is the only offered gameplay action.
expectation: The proteins and duplicated centrosomes will form a chromosome-moving spindle.

effect: The spindle is assembled as a mitosis preview, but chromosomes have not attached yet.
reaction: The timing caption clarifies that spindle assembly follows DNA copying.
reason: Use the spindle to form daughter nuclei; this is the only offered gameplay action.
expectation: The spindle will separate the copied chromosomes so two daughter nuclei can form.

effect: The copied chromosomes have separated into two nuclei, but the cytoplasm remains connected and must divide.
reaction: The time-strip clearly distinguishes nuclear division from separation of the cell.
reason: Use actin and myosin to divide the cytoplasm; this is the only offered gameplay action.
expectation: Actin and myosin will constrict the cell at the furrow, separating it into two daughter cells.

effect: The cytoplasm has separated into two stem cells, each with a complete genome; the diagram also points toward later self-renewal and differentiation.
reaction: The distinction between completed division and later differentiation is clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Using the spindle to form two nuclei was most worthwhile: the time-strip connects chromosome attachment and separation to complete genomes while showing that the cytoplasm remains connected.

leastWorthwhile.text: Building the spindle felt less engaging as a decision because it was the only gameplay action offered, although the timing caption was useful.

surprise.text: The membrane-building step showed a delivery route through the ER and Golgi rather than simply adding lipids directly to the surface.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though the broad label 'new cell proteins' leaves the connection to the specific tubulin units in the spindle somewhat implicit.

continue.text: Yes. I would be interested to see how the daughter cells take different paths toward muscle and lining, building on the distinction between division and later differentiation.
